cells.tense: You're working at it, and the working is easy to be with — steady, kept up because it keeps you near people rather than away from them.
cells.ask: offer the practice in its rough form to one person, and let the clearing it makes touch them too.
cells.core:
A small practice done alone, over and over, turns into something you can carry into a room. It's the thing that lets you sit with someone without needing to perform, because the ground under you is your own. Getting better at it hasn't pulled you away from people. It's given you somewhere to stand while you're with them.

No forcing is happening. The time you spend refining this doesn't isolate you, and it doesn't run on fear — it sends you back out with more to give. The work is carrying you rather than the other way around, and what it's clearing away is what was in the way between you and the next person. Let that be seen before it's polished.
cells.sheetLine: You're refining something with care, and the care keeps opening the door to others.
cells.verb: keeping at one small practice long enough for it to become part of you
cells.place: in the part of your life where connection with other people is made and kept

cells.tense: You're pushing the practice further out of reach, bracing for a version where it's finally good enough, and the bracing is closing the doors it was meant to open.
cells.ask: let one thing you've finished be finished, and trust that it was, without going back to check.
cells.core:
Practice done well can be a place to meet people from. You know the shape of that — the hours put in, the steadiness it gives you, the way it lets you show up without scrambling for footing. Refining something over time is how you come to trust your own hands. That part is real, and it isn't the problem.

The problem is that refining turned into proving. Solitude used to be chosen and now it feels like the only safe place, because stopping would mean facing what's left to offer. You're gripping the work past the point it needs you. What's available right now isn't more work — it's knowing it's done and setting it down.
cells.sheetLine: Refining has become proving, and it's pulling you away from the people it was for.
cells.verb: keeping at one small practice long enough for it to become part of you

cells.tense: You're standing back from practice, still at a door that's already behind you, and the doing has stopped there.
cells.ask: give one even measure of attention to what's actually yours today, small and fair, no more than that.
cells.core:
Steady practice, done in private, becomes the thing that lets you meet people without losing yourself. It's how you learn your own weight, so you can be near someone else without tipping. That kind of ground is available to anyone willing to keep showing up to something small. It doesn't ask for talent. It asks for returning.

Where you are now, the returning stopped. The quiet of doing something alone doesn't read as leading anywhere, so it reads as pulling you away, and you stay at the edge. What's missing isn't effort — it's a sense that the exchange would be fair, that you'd get back what you put in. That can be set right starting today, in one small, even trade.
cells.sheetLine: The practice stays down, and the door you're standing at is one you already walked through.
cells.verb: keeping at one small practice long enough for it to become part of you

cells.tense: You're already practicing something, in a room you're writing in without having picked up the pen to notice.
cells.ask: give one uncertain situation a loose frame, and let what you've absorbed guide the next step without a map.
cells.core:
Practice, done long enough, becomes invisible. It turns into how you hold a conversation, how you know when to step back, how you stay in the room when things are unclear. In the part of life where connection is made, that shows up as a steadiness other people feel — you can be with someone in a hard moment because you've done the small repetitions that make it possible.

What hasn't happened is you calling it yours. The skill is running under another name, so you get no credit for the hours behind it and it looks like it arrives on its own. The clarity you navigate by came from somewhere. Moving through uncertainty without forcing it open is what that practice built, and it's already working in you.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is running without your name on it, so the steadiness feels like it happens by itself.
